title: Dangerous Goods Acceptance: recording a customer's remittance
content:
## Rule
Under the Dangerous Goods Acceptance product a remittance is written with the remittance reference exactly as the customer quotes it and the amount remitted; it may not exceed the acceptance's charges due, and any excess is returned by finance and not booked. A remittance reference is recorded only once per acceptance.

## Retired clause
The earlier clause "a remittance is applied to one acceptance" is **no longer in force**. Which acceptance a remittance may be applied to follows the current basis for applying a remittance to an acceptance.

## What the charges due are
The charges due are the dangerous-goods charges owed on one acceptance: the administration fee, the surcharges, the late declaration, amendment, re-review and withdrawal fees and the penalties count in; payments and waivers count out.

## Amount recorded
The amount recorded is the lower of the amount remitted and the acceptance's charges due.

| Hypothetical case | Charges due | Remitted | Recorded | Returned by finance |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Remittance above the charges | 480.00 | 500.00 | 480.00 | 20.00 |
| Remittance below the charges | 480.00 | 300.00 | 300.00 | — |

## Points of judgement
- *May the reference be tidied up, for example by removing spaces?* No; it is written exactly as quoted.
- *May the same reference be recorded twice on the same acceptance?* No; a reference is recorded only once per acceptance.
